item.title: Partial Interval Multicover Is NP-Complete Even for Unit Intervals
item.description: arXiv:2610.41182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a interval family $\calI$, a point set $X\subseteq\mathbb R$, demands $d:X\to\Z_{\ge0}$, and $p\in\Z_{\ge0}$, partial interval multicover asks for a subfamily $S\subseteq\calI$ minimizing $|S|$ subject to $$ |\{x\in X:\dep_S(x)\ge d(x)\}|\ge p, \qquad \dep_S(x)=|\{I\in S:x\in I\}|. $$ We prove that the unweighted decision problem is NP-complete even for unit intervals, answering the open question in~\cite{Li2026}.
item.dc:creator: Mingchao Zhou, Yingli Ran, Lei Zhao, Xiangzhi Tu, Zhao Zhang

item.title: Degree Realization with Maximum Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.41810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Maximum Matching Degree Realization problem requires, for a sequence $d$ of $n$ positive integers, to compute a realizing graph(whose degree sequence corresponds to $d$) with the maximum possible matching. We present a polynomial-time algorithm for this problem. The decision version of this problem requires to determine whether a sequence $d$ admits a realization with a matching of size $\nu$ (without computing such a realization). Recently, it was shown that it can be done by verifying a series of inequalities. We improve the existing characterization by reducing the number of inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Amotz Bar-Noy, Igor Kalinichev, David Peleg, Dror Rawitz

item.title: Treedepth is NP-Hard on Planar Graphs of Maximum Degree 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.42033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Treedepth is an important parameter in algorithmic graph theory. It is known that the problem of computing the treedepth of a graph is NP-hard. It has been an open problem whether treedepth can be computed in polynomial time when the input graph is restricted to be planar, or of bounded degree. Assuming $P \neq NP$, we answer both questions in the negative: Under polynomial-time Turing reductions, it is NP-hard to compute the treedepth of planar graphs with maximum degree 3. This degree bound is best possible, since treedepth can be computed efficiently on graphs of maximum degree 2.
item.dc:creator: Kolja K\"uhn

item.title: Two choices suffice: $k$-out sampling leaves $O(n/k)$ intercomponent edges for $k\geq 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.42067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, random $k$-out sampling forms a spanning subgraph by having each vertex independently choose $k$ incident edges uniformly with replacement. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq2$, the expected number of original edges joining distinct sampled components is $O(n/k)$. This resolves the conjecture of Holm, King, Thorup, Zamir, and Zwick in its full range, improving their logarithmic sampling requirement to the optimal threshold of two choices per vertex. The bound fails for $k=1$, and the dependence $O(n/k)$ is tight up to constant factors. Our result holds with replacement and consequently also without replacement. In particular, this implies that contracting just two independent local choices per vertex suffices to reduce an arbitrary simple graph to a quotient with $O(n)$ edges in expectation, which is crucial in reducing the instance size for many contraction-based algorithms. Our proof uses switching arguments to relate intercomponent edges to bridges and a degree-weighted component potential, whose expectation we also bound with a switching argument.
item.dc:creator: Yanyu Chen, Yu Chen

item.title: The lattice of antichains of intervals: Dyck paths, level sets, and sweep dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.41385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Clarke-Cormack-Burkowski lattice $\mathcal{E}_n$ is the lattice of antichains of intervals of the chain $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the algebraic structure underlying minimal-interval semantics, a query semantics used in information retrieval. We give an explicit, elementary anti-isomorphism between $\mathcal{E}_n$ minus its top element and the Stanley lattice of Dyck words of semilength $n+1$ (an anti-isomorphism whose existence is implicit in work of Ferrari and Munarini), under which the rank of an antichain is $\binom{n+1}{2}$ minus the area of the associated Dyck word. Hence the rank generating function of $\mathcal{E}_n\setminus\{\top\}$ is the reverse of the Carlitz-Riordan $q$-Catalan polynomial. Using a local limit theorem for the area of random-walk excursions, we confirm unconditionally an asymptotic formula of Tak\'acs: the size $\lambda_n$ of the largest level set of $\mathcal{E}_n$ satisfies $\lambda_n\sim\kappa\,4^{n+1}/(n+1)^3$, where $\kappa\approx1.0807$. Finally, for the antichains of intervals of an arbitrary finite poset $P$ we study the sweep dimension, the minimum number of linear orders needed to separate every interval from every element outside it. It equals the Dushnik-Miller dimension of the lattice of convex subsets of $P$, it is the least $k$ for which $P$ maps into $\mathbb{R}^k$ so that every interval is the preimage of an upper orthant, and it lies between $\max(2,w)$ and $2w$, where $w$ is the width of $P$, both bounds being tight. Antichains of intervals embed, preserving joins, into $k$-dimensional staircase regions.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Boldi, Sebastiano Vigna

item.title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+\Theta_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.
item.dc:creator: Andrea D'Ascenzo, Riccardo Michielan

item.title: The C-3PO Framework: Algorithms for $\#\mathrm{BIS}$-Hard Problems on Graphs with Low Threshold Rank or High Girth
item.description: arXiv:2610.42011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give approximate counting and sampling algorithms for spin models on graphs of low threshold rank or high girth. Given any $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $k_\eta = k_\eta(G)$ count normalized-Laplacian eigenvalues strictly below $\eta$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, an $\varepsilon$-approximate counting algorithm outputs an estimate $\widehat Z$ of the partition function $Z$ satisfying $(1-\varepsilon)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z$ with probability at least $3/4$. An $\varepsilon$-approximate sampling algorithm outputs a configuration whose distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the target distribution. We give the following results: (a) Ferromagnetic Potts. Fix $q\ge2$ and $\eta\in(0,1]$. There exists $\beta_0(q,\eta)$ such that, for every inverse temperature $\beta\ge\beta_0$, the zero-field $q$-state Potts model admits approximate counting and sampling algorithms: (i) On arbitrary graphs in time $\exp(O(k_\eta))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) Fix $\Delta \ge 3$. On $\Delta$-regular graphs of girth $g$ in time $\exp(O(n e^{-g})) \operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (b) Bipartite hard-core. Fix $\Delta\ge3$ and $\eta\in(0,1]$. There exists $\lambda_0(\Delta,\eta)$ such that, for every fugacity $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, the hard-core model admits approximate counting and sampling: (i) On $\Delta$-regular vertex-transitive bipartite graphs in time $\exp(O (k_\eta))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) On $\Delta$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $g$ in $\exp(O(n e^{- g}))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ All four results follow from verifying the hypotheses of a new framework we call C-3PO. At a high level, the C-3PO algorithm proceeds by enumerating small cuts and reconstructing the original measure through cluster expansions. Underlying the algorithm is an improvement of subspace enumeration methods via active regression.
item.dc:creator: Ijay Narang

item.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2610.42059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $\Delta\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $\Delta$-regular graph for all $\beta<\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ where $\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $\Delta$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $\beta<\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $\Delta$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Blanca, Reza Gheissari, Heehyun Park, Xusheng Zhang

item.title: Profile and neighbourhood complexity of graphs excluding a minor and tree-structured graphs
item.description: arXiv:2501.08895v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The \emph{$r$-neighbourhood complexity} of a graph $G$ is the function counting, for a given integer $k$, the largest possible number, over all vertex-subsets $A$ of size $k$, of subsets of $A$ realized as the intersection between the $r$-neighbourhood of some vertex and $A$. A~refinement of this notion is the \emph{$r$-profile complexity}, that counts the maximum number of distinct distance-vectors from any vertex to the vertices of $A$, ignoring distances larger than~$r$. Typically, in structured graph classes such as graphs of bounded VC-dimension or chordal graphs, these functions are bounded, leading to insights into their structural properties and efficient algorithms. We improve existing bounds on the $r$-profile complexity (and thus on the $r$-neighbourhood complexity) for graphs in several structured graph classes. We show that the $r$-profile complexity of graphs excluding $K_h$ as a minor is in $O_h(r^{3h-3}k)$. For graphs of treewidth at most~$t$, we give a bound in $O_t(r^{t+1}k)$, which is tight up to a function of~$t$ as a factor. These bounds improve results of Joret and Rambaud and answer a question of their paper [Combinatorica, 2024]. We also apply our methods to other classes of bounded expansion such as graphs excluding a fixed complete graph as a subdivision. For outerplanar graphs, we can improve our treewidth bound by a factor of $r$ and conjecture that a similar improvement holds for graphs with bounded simple treewidth. For graphs of treelength at most~$\ell$, we give the upper bound of $O(k(r^2(\ell+1)^k))$, which we improve to $O\left (k\cdot (r 2^k + r^2k^2) \right)$ in the case of chordal graphs and $O(k^2r)$ for interval graphs. Our bounds also imply relations between the order, diameter and metric dimension of graphs in these classes, improving results from [Beaudou et al., SIDMA 2017].
item.dc:creator: Laurent Beaudou, Jan Bok, Florent Foucaud, Daniel A. Quiroz, Jean-Florent Raymond

item.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
item.description: arXiv:1307.2827v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.
item.dc:creator: Marko Puljic

item.title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
item.description: arXiv:1507.06053v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $\sigma(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Han Xiao

item.title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
item.description: arXiv:2405.13302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds.
item.dc:creator: Wonwoo Kang, Heehyun Park

item.title: Characterizing the optimum bases of a convex geometry using quasi-closed hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.14615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimizing an implicational base of a closure system consists in turning this implicational base into an equivalent one with premises and conclusions as small as possible. This task is known to be hard in general but tractable for a number of classes of closure systems. In particular, several classes of convex geometries are known to have tractable optimization, while the problem was recently claimed to remain hard in general convex geometries. Continuing this line of research, we give a characterization of the optimum bases of a convex geometry in terms of what we call quasi-closed hypergraphs. We then use this characterization to show that when each quasi-closed hypergraph has disjoint edges, any implicational base of the convex geometry can be optimized in polynomial time with existing minimization and reduction algorithms. Finally, we prove that this property applies to double-shelling convex geometries, $D$-geometries, convex geometries with the $n$-Carousel property and $q$-acceptant convex geometries, thus unifying and extending the existing results regarding the tractability of optimization.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Meunier, Lhouari Nourine, Simon Vilmin

item.title: On the Column Number of Delta-Modular Matrices: an $O(m^2 \Delta)$ Bound via the Shifted Heller Constant
item.description: arXiv:2608.06215v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we build on the analysis initiated by Averkov and Schymura (2022) and prove that the shifted Heller constant for matrices with $m$ rows is at most $m^2 + m$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Consequently, the number of distinct columns of a $\Delta$-modular matrix $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ of rank $m$ is at most $O(m^2 \Delta)$. This improves upon the earlier bounds of $O(m^4 \Delta)$ and $O(m^2 \Delta^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Elizaveta Pribytkova, Dmitrii Gribanov, Dmitrii Taletskii, Stanislav Moiseev

item.title: A proof of Wang's planar $D$-coloring conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33322v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove Wang's planar $D$-coloring conjecture. A $D$-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a $D$-coloring with $9$ colors if $\Delta=4$, $10$ colors if $\Delta=5$, and $2\Delta-1$ colors if $\Delta\ge6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $\Delta\le5$ and $\Delta\ge33$. We prove the sharp bound $2\Delta-1$ for every $\Delta\ge6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $\Delta=6$ is computer-assisted.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma
